content: Due to the extensive nature of the content, I will provide a concise yet detailed version of the key points. Disclaimer WikiDoc does not guarantee the validity of its content. It is not a substitute for professional healthcare providers and is intended solely as an educational resource. The drug-related content is based on FDA package inserts, the National Library of Medicine, and clinical guidelines. WikiDoc does not endorse the use of any medication or device outside of its approved labeling. Overview of Sandbox gc4 (Remdesivir) Sandbox gc4, an adenosine nucleotide prodrug, is authorized under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for treating suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections in hospitalized adults and pediatric patients with severe disease. Severe disease is defined as oxygen saturation (SpO2) ≤ 94% on room air, requiring supplemental oxygen, mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Common Adverse Reactions: Nausea Constipation Fever (pyrexia) Acute respiratory failure Anemia (reduced hemoglobin) Acute kidney injury (e.g., decreased eGFR, increased creatinine) Hyperglycemia (elevated blood glucose) Elevated transaminases Adult Indications and Dosage Indications: Remdesivir is authorized for hospitalized adults with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection requiring intravenous (IV) administration. Dosage: Day 1: A single 200 mg loading dose via IV infusion. Day 2 onward: 100 mg once daily via IV infusion. Duration: 10 days for patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation or ECMO. 5 days for patients not requiring invasive support, extendable to 10 days if clinically indicated. Pediatric Indications and Dosage Indications: Remdesivir is authorized for hospitalized pediatric patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection, defined similarly to adults. Dosage: For patients weighing 3.5 kg to less than 40 kg, the dose is weight-based (mg/kg). Only the lyophilized powder formulation should be used for patients under 40 kg due to the higher tonicity of the solution concentrate. Duration: 10 days for those requiring invasive mechanical ventilation or ECMO. 5 days for those not requiring invasive support, extendable to 10 days if needed. Contraindications Remdesivir is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any of its components. Warnings and Precautions 1. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Infusion-related and anaphylactic reactions have been reported. Symptoms may include hypotension, tachycardia, bradycardia, dyspnea, wheezing, angioedema, rash, nausea, vomiting, sweating, and shivering. Slower infusion rates (up to 120 minutes) may reduce these risks. Discontinue immediately if significant hypersensitivity occurs. 2. Elevated Transaminases: Transaminase elevations have been observed in clinical trials and may be related to COVID-19 itself. Baseline and daily hepatic function tests are recommended. Do not initiate remdesivir if ALT is ≥ 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN). Discontinue if ALT rises ≥ 5 times ULN or if liver inflammation symptoms occur. 3. Drug Interactions: Co-administration with chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine is not recommended due to reduced antiviral activity. Use in Specific Populations 1. Pregnancy: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk to the mother and fetus. Animal studies have shown no adverse effects on embryofetal development at exposures up to 4 times the human dose. 2. Nursing Mothers: The presence of remdesivir in human milk is unknown. Animal studies suggest potential transfer through milk. Weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against the mother’s clinical need for remdesivir. 3. Pediatric Use: Safety and efficacy in pediatric patients have not been fully established. Dosing is based on physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling. 4. Renal Impairment: Not recommended for patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min or neonates with serum creatinine ≥ 1 mg/dL unless benefits outweigh risks. Monitor renal function daily. 5. Hepatic Impairment: Use with caution. Perform baseline and daily hepatic function tests. 6. Geriatric Use: Exercise caution due to the higher likelihood of comorbidities and reduced organ function in elderly patients. Administration and Monitoring 1. Testing Prior to Treatment: Determine eGFR in patients > 28 days old. Determine serum creatinine in neonates (7–28 days old). Perform hepatic function tests before and during treatment. 2. Preparation and Administration: Administer via IV infusion only. Do not use intramuscularly. Reconstitute lyophilized powder with sterile water and dilute in 0.9% sodium chloride. Use aseptic technique to prevent contamination. Administer immediately after preparation when possible. Adverse Reactions 1. Clinical Trials: Common adverse events include nausea, acute respiratory failure, increased ALT, and constipation. Serious adverse events (SAEs) such as respiratory failure occurred in 5% of remdesivir-treated patients compared to 8% in placebo groups. 2. Postmarketing Experience: Limited data are available.
